vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-p2p
Version: 0.3.0

The skill automates the deployment of a P2P communication portal, which involves high-risk operations such as remote server management via SSH, execution of sudo commands, and modification of local OpenClaw configuration files (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json). Scripts like install.py and scripts/deploy_portal.py handle sensitive credentials (SSH keys, API keys) and perform complex system configurations on a remote VPS. While these actions are aligned with the stated purpose of establishing a decentralized communication network, the broad execution privileges and the use of a weak hardcoded default password ('AgentP2P2024') in scripts/deploy_portal.py and src/main.py present a significant security risk and attack surface.

llm.summary: The skill largely matches a P2P portal/deploy tool but contains inconsistencies and automation that could expose or misuse sensitive tokens/credentials (undeclared env vars, automated token exchange/confirmation, and a hard-coded SECRET_KEY), so review carefully before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code and docs implement a portal deployment + local client that maintains WebSocket connections and exchanges API keys/tokens — this is broadly coherent with the 'P2P portal' purpose. However the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or credentials while the code expects and uses several sensitive environment variables (e.g., OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL, AGENTP2P_API_KEY/AGENTP2P_TOKEN). That metadata omission is an inconsistency.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the user to run install.py which asks for an SSH private key and will SSH into the VPS and perform privileged actions (install packages, configure nginx, create systemd service). The client code additionally polls guest messages, extracts verification codes and tokens, auto-confirms verification by POSTing to other portals, and posts notifications to the OpenClaw gateway. Those automated behaviors go beyond 'just connect WebSocket' — they can cause credentials/tokens to be transmitted and actions to be taken without fine-grained user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external download URL is used; install is instruction-driven (install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py). The installer can run pip to install paramiko and will SSH into the user's VPS and execute remote commands. While not an outright red flag, remote privileged operations and automatic dependency installs deserve caution because they run commands on your infrastructure.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The package metadata lists no required env vars, but client.py expects and enforces several sensitive variables: AGENTP2P_API_KEY / AGENTP2P_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL. OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN (a gateway/hook bearer token) is particularly sensitive: the client uses it to call the local OpenClaw gateway to 'wake' the main session and will include message contents (including Tokens) in those notifications. Requiring these secrets without declaring them is a mismatch and increases risk of credential exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not set always:true and is user-invocable by default. The installer writes files under ~/.openclaw and can configure a systemd service on the remote VPS (requires sudo on the VPS). The installer also writes a systemd service with a hard-coded SECRET_KEY (agent-p2p-shared-key-2024), which creates a shared secret across deployments and is a security weakness but not an automatic privilege escalation on the local machine.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill will deploy server-side code to a VPS using your SSH key and will run a local client that expects and uses OpenClaw gateway hooks tokens and agent API keys — but the package metadata does not declare these requirements. Before installing:

- Do not supply your SSH private key to any script unless you fully trust and have reviewed the remote commands the installer will run. Consider creating a dedicated deploy key with limited access.
- The local client expects OPENCLAW_HOOKS_TOKEN and will use it to post message contents (including tokens) to your OpenClaw gateway. Only set this token if you understand and accept that messages (and any extracted 'Token' strings) may be forwarded to the main session.
- The installer writes a systemd service on the VPS with a hard-coded SECRET_KEY; this allows token forgery across installations. Consider changing the SECRET_KEY to a random secret after deployment.
- The client automatically parses guest messages for URLs, verification codes, and tokens and can auto-confirm codes and exchange tokens with other portals. That automates credential exchange and could be abused if someone posts crafted content to your guest message area. If you want stricter control, disable or audit the auto-confirm/auto-exchange code paths.

If you still want to try it, review the install.py, scripts/deploy_portal.py and client.py code line-by-line (especially parts that send HTTP requests and that call the OpenClaw gateway) or run the installer in a safe isolated environment (throwaway VPS, dedicated deploy key) first. If you are not comfortable auditing the code, treat this skill as high-risk and avoid installing it on production or systems with sensitive credentials.
